'''Sheila May Edmonds''' (1 April 1916 – 2 September 2002) was a British [[mathematician]], a [[Lecturer]] at the [[University of Cambridge]], and Vice-Principal of [[Newnham College, Cambridge|Newnham College]] from 1960 to 1981.

== Early life and education ==
Born in [[Kingston, Kent]], Edmonds studied at [[Wimbledon High School]] and entered Newnham College, Cambridge in 1935 to study for the [[Mathematical Tripos]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite news|url=http://www-history.mcs.st-and.ac.uk/Obits/Edmonds.html|title= Senior Cambridge mathematician who taught and inspired generations of women |newspaper=[[The Times]]|year=2002|via=MacTutor History of Mathematics Archive|access-date=2016-10-11}}</ref><ref name=":1" /> At this time women could attend lectures and sit examinations but were not permitted to graduate with a degree.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/at-last-a-degree-of-honour-for-900-cambridge-women-1157056.html|title=At last, a degree of honour for 900 Cambridge women|last=Chambers|first=Suzanna|date=1998-05-31|newspaper=The Independent|language=en-GB|access-date=2016-10-11}}</ref> She had an excellent undergraduate career and finished Part II as a "[[Wrangler (University of Cambridge)|Wrangler]]", Cambridge nomenclature for a student achieving a First Class award. Edmonds followed this with a Distinction in [[Part III of the Mathematical Tripos|Part III]], and then studied for a [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] with [[G. H. Hardy]]. During her doctoral research she spent a year at [[Westfield College]], London, and a year at the [[University of Paris]]. She was awarded PhD for her dissertation "Some Multiplication Problems" in 1944.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://webserver.newn.cam.ac.uk/about-newnham/college-history/biographies/content/sheila-edmonds-long|title=Biographies: Sheila May Edmonds 1916–2002|last=Siklos|first=Stephen|publisher=Newnham College|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161012075229/http://webserver.newn.cam.ac.uk/about-newnham/college-history/biographies/content/sheila-edmonds-long|archive-date=2016-10-12|url-status=dead|access-date=2016-10-11}}</ref>

== Career ==
Edmonds's first papers were published while she was studying for her PhD, with two in 1942 on [[series (mathematics)|infinite series]] and on [[Fourier transform]]s. These led to a series of papers over the following years, exploring these topics and building on her PhD research into [[Parseval's theorem]].<ref name=":1">{{MacTutor|id=Edmonds}}</ref>

She was a dedicated teacher, supervising students in all branches of [[pure mathematics|pure]] and [[applied mathematics]], as well as lecturing courses in the Mathematical Tripos. Edmonds served on the University Faculty Board of Mathematics for many years, and was its chair in 1975 and 1976.<ref name=":0" />

In 1960, Edmonds was appointed Vice-Principal of Newnham, one of the senior offices of the college, a post which she held until her retirement in 1981. She also served on the [[University of Cambridge Local Examinations Syndicate]] and the boards of governors of several schools including [[Roedean School|Rodean]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.newn.cam.ac.uk/about/history/biographies/|title=Significant contributors in the history of Newnham College|publisher=Newnham College|language=en-GB|access-date=2016-10-11}}</ref>
